x: After the runners had gone away for the second time, I thought the prospect of the "Bels" winning a very good one, but some fine running by the Surrey A.C., who had Belton and Newton second and third respectively, backed up by their tail men, secured them first team honours.

These times placed us 2nd 4th 5th and 6th on the all-time list, ahead of anything Hayward, Walsh, Newton and Allan had ever done. The sixth man, Charley Chase of J'burg did 6:30.42 - he hadn't been nominated for the S.A. team and spent four days before the race drinking in Durban bars!
Those men who, through the passage of time, have been proved right were ridiculed in their day (Newton, Cerutty etc.) but those who have been proved wrong invariably get away with it.
